sections_inspected: Chapter 12, "Autonomy, Oligarchy, Statesman: Weber, Castoriadis and the Fragility of Politics," pp. 235–261, especially the sections "Non-legitimate Domination in the Work of Max Weber—Open and Closed Circulations of the Political" and "On Plato’s Statesman: Castoriadis, Reflexive Closure and the Challenge to Politics"
scope_outcomes.criterion: A held secondary text must make an anchored argument or interpretation about Max Weber, rather than merely mention or cite him.
scope_outcomes.basis: The inspected chapter directly reconstructs Weber’s account of the city, patrimonialism, oligarchic and plebeian political forms, closure, circulation, autonomy, democracy and tyranny.
limitations: The findings concern Rundell’s reading in the supplied text and do not establish engagement by Dylan Riley.
The source is not evidence of Riley’s complete reception or of Weber’s entire reception.

The source also contains a subsequent chapter by Toula Nicolacopoulos and George Vassilacopoulos; no additional row was drawn from that chapter because the supplied passage begins its discussion of Castoriadis rather than presenting a developed argument about Weber.
